title: Who captivates you?
subtitle: A few minutes. No right answers.

steps.body:
The anima — the inner feminine in men — tends to project outward onto women who seem to carry what we're missing. The captivation isn't only about her.

It's partly about you.
Before we begin — take a breath. Let yourself arrive.

steps.title: Who comes to mind?
steps.body: Someone whose presence pulls at you in a way that's hard to explain — a woman you're drawn to, fascinated by, or can't stop thinking about. Even someone from the past.

steps.title: What specifically draws you to her?
steps.body: Not looks alone. What quality — how she moves through the world, what she seems to embody, what becomes possible in you when you're near her.

steps.title: How strong is the pull?
steps.body: The strength of the pull is information — it points at how much you want what she seems to carry.
That landed with some weight. Take one breath here before going on — there's no rush.

steps.title: Is there a sense that {subject|she} could complete something in you?
steps.body: What would you have — or become — if {subject|she} were in your life? Say it plainly, even if it sounds like too much.

steps.title: What would it mean to find {quality|that quality} in yourself?
steps.body: Not to stop wanting connection. But what if you stopped needing {subject|her} to carry {quality|it} for you — and let yourself carry it instead?

exit.body:
The pull you feel toward {subject|her} is real. So is what it's pointing at — something in you that wants to come alive.

The work isn't to stop the longing. It's to let it lead somewhere inside.
